reconcile.note: Adam Clarke reads Sarah's laughter in Genesis 18 as initial doubt that gave way to the belief Hebrews 11:11 later credits.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible ("Did Sarah have faith that she would conceive?", skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/sarah.html) (1999).

sides.snippet: Sarah laughed within herself, saying, \"After I have grown old will I have pleasure, my lord being old also?\"
sides.verseText: Sarah laughed within herself, saying, \"After I have grown old will I have pleasure, my lord being old also?\"

sides.snippet: By faith, even Sarah herself received power to conceive
sides.verseText: By faith, even Sarah herself received power to conceive, and she bore a child when she was past age, since she counted him faithful who had promised.
